newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks advance cautiously on rate concerns.
newsitem.headline: French stocks advance cautiously on rate concerns.

text.p: French shares finished higher on Tuesday, the first day of the monthly account, but the market's advance was cautious ahead of an anticipated increase in U.S. interest rates and a string of upcoming corporate results.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 14.41 points, or 0.7 percent, at 2,081.50, while the CAC-40 September futures contract rose 14.50 points to 2,086.
* Canal Plus finished up 1.34 percent at 1,207 on a 16.6 percent rise in first-half profit. The stock hit a high of 1,219 after a source close to the group disclosed the result.
Sources said media group Havas had retained Societe Generale to buy a significant part of Canal Plus's capital for up to 1,200 francs per share.

* Usinor Sacilor recouped an early fall on a big drop in its first-half profit and closed up 4.46 percent at 78.45 francs as investors were heartened by bullish medium-term forecast. The company predicted a higher first-half 1997 profit.

* Saint-Gobain rose 3.11 percent to 664 francs after meetings with portfolio managers. They said the group told them summer activity was brisk at the Poliet home improvements unit and the Brazilian market was holding up well.
They said Saint-Gobain also discussed asset sales plans. The group said it reiterated comments made previously.
* GTM Entrepose, a unit of Lyonnaise des Eaux, fell 7.26 percent to 254.10 francs after reporting a first-half loss. Lyonnaise slipped 0.49 percent.
Analysts expect Lyonnaise to report a first-half profit of around 700-730 million francs on Thursday, up from 506 million.
* Danone rose 2.09 percent after announcing a chilled juice venture with Coca-Cola Foods.
* Comptoirs Modernes rose 4.04 percent to 2,448 francs in heavy trading.

The stock hit a year high of 2,474 francs after block trades totalling 0.48 percent of its capital. There was talk Carrefour may be bolstering its 23 percent stake in Comptoirs but Carrefour denied the rumour.

* Sidel fell 6.25 percent to 300 francs after the bottling machinery company reported a 47 percent fall in first-half profit. Traders said several analysts cut their earnings forecasts after the weaker-than-expected results.
* Other companies reporting results this week include Lafarge, LVMH, Axa, Lagardere and Alcatel.
